newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin meets visiting Indian prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin meets visiting Indian prime minister.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Tuesday Russia was committed to maintaining close relations with India which it sees as a stabilising force in Asia, Interfax news agency said.
"We have been friends for many decades and we remain friends," Yeltsin told visiting Indian Prime Minister H.P. Deve Gowda. "India remains a stabilising force in its region."

Deve Gowda was also due to hold talks with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin. India and Russia are due to sign several agreements on avoiding double taxation, customs cooperation, extradition of criminals, mutual legal assistance in criminal affairs and a consular convention.
Russian officials have said that military and technical cooperation between the two countries was high on the agenda.
Moscow has traditionally had close relations with India, especially strong in the 1960s and 1970s when New Delhi was involved in conflicts with China and U.S. ally Pakistan.

The weakness of post-Soviet Russia made special relations with it less attractive for India. This became clear in 1993 when Moscow postponed, under U.S. pressure, a $300 million contract on the sale of rocket boosters to India.

But bilateral links have started improving lately as Russia, in a deadlock with the West over NATO plans to expand eastwards, has begun focusing more on relations with traditional partners to its south and east.
The Russian space agency Glavkosmos said on Monday that Moscow would start supplying rocket boosters to India later this year, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Interfax news agency quoted Oleg Sidorenko, deputy head of arms trader Rosvooruzheniye, as saying the two countries were planning to launch a new long-term programme of military cooperation in the year 2000.

Detailed figures of Russian-Indian arms trade are not officially published. But military officials have said that last year's $1.8 billion contract to sell India 40 modern SU-30MK jet fighters was the biggest between them so far.
Russia officially sells arms to 51 countries, but military officials say about 60 percent of sales go to India or China.
